column7: CANDIDATES SUPPLIED, BUT THEY ANSWER A DIFFERENT QUESTION. Gu 2017 (root length/diameter image analysis), Parida 2021 (specific root length and specific root area under water stress), Wang 2024 (root characteristics vs seedling age) and Li 2019 PeerJ (fine-root length, surface area, volume, biomass) are all ROOT morphology. Two problems: (i) the air-exchange term takes NO root contribution at all - the derivation states there is no volatilisation from roots - so root area cannot bound it; (ii) root specific area enters this model only through a_R, which is lumped into kappa_d = a_R * P_d_eff and is documented as non-separable without inhibitor data, so a value for it unlocks nothing on its own. Parida's SRA is also figure-only (Fig. 2d) and on a dry-weight basis.

column1: DEFINITION NOTE - PARTLY RESOLVED by A1. Read before adopting any lipid number.

The L in K_PW = W + L*a*Kow^b is an OPERATIONALLY DEFINED octanol-like phase calibrated so the expression reproduces measured RCF. A1 settled the basis question: Li/Chiou 2019 use exactly this expression, their f_lip is FRESH weight (dry-basis reports converted at 90 percent root water), and on that basis cereal roots are 0.53-1.14 percent - which corroborates the 1 percent the repo runs. What A1 did NOT settle, and in fact sharpened, is the LEVEL. Briggs' fitted lipid term L*a = 10^-1.52 implies L = 2.47 percent fresh at the conventional a = 1.22, i.e. 2.5x the measured cereal value; and Briggs 1982 reports NO lipid content at all (verified at source - he attributes the 0.82 floor to root WATER and never measures a lipid), so both figures are inferences from a paper that measured neither. The excess is most plausibly NON-LIPID sorption - cell wall and lignin, which this repo's PFAS side carries as f_cw*K_cw and lists as GAP A, and which the neutral composition sets to zero. Consequence for anyone tempted to substitute a number here: the rice root currently runs 2.5x BELOW the Briggs anchor it claims, that costs log10 RMSE 0.266 vs 0.111 on Briggs' own barley rows, and raising L to fix it improves two tables and degrades the only rice one. See validation/li2019_rcf_apriori.py and the DEFAULT-UNCHANGED decision it records. The straw case is unchanged and still cautionary: 0.14-1.0 percent dry weight as crude fat (ether extract) but 3.4 percent dry weight as dichloromethane extractives (A2), a 3-24x spread that is a difference of DEFINITION, not of measurement quality.
